issues.title: Fourier valuation uses incompatible transform orientations
issues.failure_explanation: The proposition claims that its integral equals the discounted expectation of P(X_T). With the old definitions, however, the product of Φ_X(y+iR) and the positive-sign transform of P imposes x+X_T=0 under Fourier inversion. The damping factors then cancel at x=-X_T, so the right-hand side represents the discounted expectation of P(-X_T), which materially differs from the option value for a nonsymmetric payoff.
issues.overall_effect: The literal valuation formula and the resulting interpretation of g as an option-pricing integrand are wrong. The later VG and NIG propositions remain valid as generic integral-transformation identities for the defined g and therefore are not dependent affected formal results.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the Fourier convention already forced by the old payoff-transform formulas and analyticity strips: define P̂(z) = ∫ exp(-i z^T x)P(x) dx and replace the payoff damping condition exp(-R^T x)P(x) by exp(R^T x)P(x), retaining the same regularity and integrability requirements. Keep the positive-sign definition of Φ, the valuation formula, and g unchanged. Standard Fourier inversion then gives the discounted expectation of P(X_T).
issues.why_classification: The Gamma-function payoff transforms and their stated strips in the old source are precisely those for the negative-sign payoff transform, so the intended convention is determined internally rather than inferred only from the revision. Correcting the two coordinated sign occurrences restores the cited valuation identity without repairing a proof, adding a premise, weakening the result, or changing any downstream construction; this is a transcriptional convention error.

issues.title: RQMC error estimator centers at an undefined quantity
issues.failure_explanation: Equation eq:RQMC_estimator defines the average over S randomizations as Q^{RQMC}_{N,S,d}[g], but rqmc_error subtracts Q^{RQMC}_{N,d}[g], for which the old source gives no definition. The sample variance across randomizations must be centered at their S-shift average.
issues.overall_effect: The reported statistical-error certificate is undefined as written, although the underlying RQMC point estimator remains well-defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the undefined centering term Q^{RQMC}_{N,d}[g] in rqmc_error by Q^{RQMC}_{N,S,d}[g], the average of the S per-randomization estimates defined immediately above.
issues.why_classification: The omitted S index is uniquely forced by the preceding estimator and by the definition of sample variance. The correction is purely notational and requires no mathematical argument or change to the estimator or its guarantee.

issues.title: Generic dependent-CDF inverse is not a valid domain transformation

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The integration problem in \eqref{eq:literature_integrand} assumes an independence structure

issues.failure_explanation: An ordinary joint multivariate CDF is scalar-valued and does not have the vector inverse asserted in eq:change_of_variable. If Psi is instead interpreted as the vector of marginal CDFs, its componentwise inverse has a Jacobian determined by the marginal densities, not by the joint density psi when the components are dependent. Thus the old inverse and Jacobian contract is valid only with additional transport structure, such as independence or an explicit factor construction.
issues.overall_effect: The generic transformed-pricing equation is not justified for an arbitrary dependent proposal distribution. The old VG and NIG propositions derive their variance-mixture transformations independently, so their formal identities are not dependent affected results.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the asserted inverse of an ordinary joint CDF by an explicitly supplied transport T from the unit cube to the proposal distribution. State that T pushes uniform measure forward to the density ψ; equivalently, for a differentiable bijection, require |det DT(u)| = 1/ψ(T(u)). Then write the transformed integral as ∫_[0,1]^d g(T(u))/ψ(T(u)) du. Use componentwise marginal ICDFs only under independence, and use an inverse Rosenblatt map or the paper's explicit normal-factor or mixture transports for dependent proposals.
issues.why_classification: This is not a typo because an ordinary multivariate CDF genuinely has the wrong type and there is no unique inverse. Nevertheless, the standard transport formulation is a short, local, source-supported correction that preserves the transformed-pricing identity, all concrete dependent-model constructions, and all rates and conclusions; no new core proof architecture or downstream formal-result repair is needed.

issues.title: Gaussian transformation proposal is not normalized
issues.failure_explanation: For tilde sigma_j>0, integrating the prescribed expression gives sqrt(2pi) tilde sigma_j divided by sqrt(2) tilde sigma_j, namely sqrt(pi), rather than one. It therefore cannot be the claimed Gaussian proposal density or generate the asserted CDF/ICDF and Jacobian transformation.
issues.overall_effect: Taken literally, the independent-GBM domain-transformation construction does not define a probability distribution, so its ICDF interface and density-ratio identity are invalid. The later mixture propositions use independently specified normal random variables and are not defeated by this transcription error.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor π wherever the independent Gaussian proposal is defined, so that ψ_j(y_j) = exp(-y_j^2/(2 tildeσ_j^2))/sqrt(2π tildeσ_j^2), and use the corresponding normalized Gaussian CDF and ICDF. No boundary-growth condition needs to change.
issues.why_classification: Normalization uniquely forces the missing π, and the later density-ratio calculation already uses sqrt(2π tildeσ_j^2). Thus the reasoning reflects the normalized Gaussian and the displayed denominator is a transcription error rather than a defective construction.

issues.title: VG Student-t degrees-of-freedom prescription has the wrong direction
issues.failure_explanation: The old calculation establishes boundedness only when tilde nu is at most bar nu=2T/nu-1, but the executable parameter prescription sets tilde nu=bar nu+epsilon for arbitrary epsilon>=0. Thus every allowed epsilon>0 makes the characteristic-function-to-density ratio diverge at the boundary.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised family of independent-VG transformations includes proposals that introduce the very boundary singularity the construction is intended to avoid. Proposition prop:vg_proposition remains a valid mixture identity for any positive degrees of freedom and is not itself affected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the independent-VG prescription as 0 < tildeν ≤ barν, where barν = 2T/ν - 1 and barν > 0. Equivalently, set tildeν = barν - ε with 0 ≤ ε < barν. Delete or qualify any plus-ε or floor prescription that selects tildeν > barν, while retaining the stated scale formula and the unrestricted mixture identity.
issues.why_classification: The old source's own limit calculation explicitly proves that boundedness requires tildeν ≤ barν, and its dependent-case discussion uses the same downward direction. The isolated plus sign is therefore uniquely forced to be a minus sign; the removed values cannot satisfy the advertised boundary-boundedness property, so correcting the prescription surrenders no coherent guarantee and requires no new analysis.

issues.title: NIG hybrid estimator uses an undefined mixing variable
issues.failure_explanation: In the finite estimator, the only outer mixing values are the Gauss–Laguerre nodes y_m, but both g and psi_lap are evaluated at w times the normal factor. No w is bound by any sum or surrounding integral there, so the estimator is not executable and does not instantiate the integrand in the preceding mixture representation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated hybrid numerical estimator cannot be evaluated as written. The preceding formal mixture identity prop:nig_proposition remains valid because its outer integral correctly binds w.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the finite Gauss–Laguerre/RQMC estimator, replace every unbound occurrence of w inside g and ψ_lap by the current outer quadrature node y_m. Thus both functions are evaluated at y_m times the normal factor, consistently with the outer density factor already evaluated at y_m.
issues.why_classification: The preceding integral binds w as the outer variable, while the finite outer sum binds only y_m. Substitution of y_m is uniquely forced by the quadrature discretization and makes the estimator executable without changing its construction, result, or guarantee.
